teaser: The fitting room mirror is cracked down one side, and the curtain won't quite close. You are a 5, carrying the pull toward the next room, the next version of the day, and an ESFJ, built to belong, to keep a group fed and seated and warm. Most fives treat belonging as a cage to keep circling, looking for the latch. You treat it as the thing you host. The tension here isn't between wanting people and wanting out; it's between wanting everyone comfortable and wanting the door left open, just in case.
